subject: general
question: The guardian of the Constitution of India is:
solution:
The correct answer is **the Supreme Court**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Judiciary is permitted by the Constitution to review the legislation passed by Parliament; hence the **Supreme Court** serves as the guardian of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Supreme Court has the authority to review and annul a law passed by the legislature if it is ultra vires certain constitutional requirements, according to **Article 14 of the Constitution**.
 
• By ruling any measure that violates fundamental rights unconstitutional, the Supreme Court also serves as the **guardian **of these rights.
 
• According to **Article 32 of the Constitution**, the Supreme Court may issue writs to compel adherence to fundamental rights if it discovers that they are being violated.
 
• These writs are of the** Habeas Corpus**, **Mandamus**,** Quo Warranto**, **Prohibition**, and **Certiorari varieties**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Lok Sabha, or House of the People** in official usage, is the name of the** lower house of India's bicameral Parliament.**
 
• The **president of a nation** generally performs the roles of the official head of state, head of the executive branch, and pivotal leader of the nation.
 
• According to its **constitution, India's bicameral Parliament's upper chamber **is referred to as the **Rajya Sabha or Council of States.**
